glosses: das Mauerwerk oder ein Bauelement an der Unterseite abschrägen

examples.text: Um beim Hinaufgehen dem Fusse eine sichere Trittfläche zu bieten, kann man auch das Stufenprofil nach der schmalen Seite zu stärker unterschneiden, […] wie das schon bei mittelalterlichen Wendel- und Spindeltreppen geschehen ist.
An den Rankengiebeln in Athen sind die Einzelformen perspektivisch gedreht und stark unterschnitten, jedoch nicht mit dem Grund verwachsen.
An ihrem höchsten Punkt unterschneidet die Kehle diese obere Platte.

glosses: den Ball auf die untere Hälfte schlagen, sodass in Flugrichtung eine Rückwärtsdrehung des Balles entsteht

examples.text: David ließ sich nicht genug Zeit für den Schlag und unterschnitt den Ball.
Den zweiten Slyce von der Grundlinie unterschneidet er aber zu deutlich und lässt den Ball hinter die Grundlinie ins Aus fliegen.

Das tut nicht weh, und wenn man sich geschickt anstellt und den Ball unterschneidet, kriegt er den so genannten Effet, das heißt, man kann seine Flugbahn beeinflussen, die nur übers Netz und ins gegnerische Spielfeld führen muss.

translations.source_sense_description: das Mauerwerk oder ein Bauelement an der Unterseite abschrägen

glosses: A cut made in the lower part of something; the material so removed.
The notch cut in a tree to direct its fall when being felled.
The underside of a sirloin of beef; the fillet.
A hairstyle that is shaved or clipped short on the sides and kept long on the top.

examples.text: Maybe it’s true that “the Left can’t meme,” if “the Left” refers to the earnest suburban revolutionary with an undercut and a nose ring who typically stalks your replies on X.

glosses: A blow dealt upward.
A section of a mold or pattern with negative draft angle
A pit stop strategy in which a driver seeks to gain an advantage over someone by pitting before them and using fresh tyres to make up time.
The continuation of the saddle of a rabbit's coat toward the front legs.
To sell (something) at a lower price, or to work for lower wages, than a competitor.

examples.text: The fact that, to cover low tariffs on bulk commodities, the railways have to charge very high rates on high-value goods, such as manufactures, has provided road operators with a golden opportunity to undercut the railway.

glosses: To create an overhang by cutting away material from underneath.
To undermine.

examples.text: Though Bane’s sing-song voice gives his pronouncements a funny lilt, he doesn’t have any of the Joker’s deranged wit, and Nolan isn’t interested in undercutting his seriousness for the sake of a breezier entertainment.

glosses: To strike a heavy blow upward.
To employ the undercut strategy.
To downplay or minimize.

examples.text: This was a very generous way of describing the swarm of cables, kit-bashed thaumatic cores, Noogenic foci and para-technological inverters, all surrounded by an astoundingly complex cognitohazardous sigil and multiple ontological anchors. This, simultaneously, simplified the interdisciplinary effort that had swelled in a miniscule amount of time, and undercut the sheer conceptual impact this could leave in all of their respective fields.

glosses: Produced by undercutting.
Designed so as to cut from the underside.
Having the parts in relief cut under.

translations.source_sense_description: den Ball auf die untere Hälfte schlagen, sodass in Flugrichtung eine Rückwärtsdrehung des Balles entsteht

glosses: That which is thin and broad.

examples.text: I pulled in hand over hand on the cord, and when I judged myself near enough, rose at infinite risk to about half my height and thus commanded the roof and a slice of the interior of the cabin.

glosses: A thin, broad piece cut off.

examples.text: a slice of bacon; a slice of cheese; a slice of bread
Jim was munching on a slice of toast.

glosses: An amount of anything.

examples.text: Blackpool, chasing a seventh win in 17 league matches, simply could not contain Sunderland's rampant attack and had to resort to a combination of last-ditch defending, fine goalkeeping and a large slice of fortune.

glosses: A piece of pizza, shaped like a sector of a circle.

examples.text: For breakfast, lunch, or dinner, the best Guido meal is a slice and a Coke.

glosses: A snack consisting of pastry with savoury filling.

examples.text: I bought a ham and cheese slice at the service station.

glosses: A broad, thin piece of plaster.
A knife with a thin, broad blade for taking up or serving fish; also, a spatula for spreading anything, as paint or ink.
A salver, platter, or tray.

A plate of iron with a handle, forming a kind of chisel, or a spadelike implement, variously proportioned, and used for various purposes, as for stripping the planking from a vessel's side, for cutting blubber from a whale, or for stirring a fire of coals; a slice bar; a peel; a fire shovel.
One of the wedges by which the cradle and the ship are lifted clear of the building blocks to prepare for launching.
A removable sliding bottom to a galley.
A shot that (for the right-handed player) curves unintentionally to the right. See fade, hook, draw.
A kind of cut shot where the bat makes an obtuse angle with the batter.
Any of a class of heavy cakes or desserts made in a tray and cut out into squarish slices.
A section of image taken of an internal organ using MRI (magnetic resonance imaging), CT (computed tomography), or various forms of x-ray.
A hawk's or falcon's dropping which squirts at an angle other than vertical. (See mute.)
A contiguous portion of an array.
To cut into slices.

examples.text: Slice the cheese thinly.

glosses: To cut with an edge using a drawing motion.

examples.text: The knife left sliced his arm.

glosses: To clear (e.g. a fire, or the grate bars of a furnace) by means of a slice bar.
To hit the shuttlecock with the racket at an angle, causing it to move sideways and downwards.
To hit a shot that slices (travels from left to right for a right-handed player).
To angle the blade so that it goes too deeply into the water when starting to take a stroke.
To kick the ball so that it goes in an unintended direction, at too great an angle or too high.

examples.text: Chris Brunt sliced the spot-kick well wide but his error was soon forgotten as Olsson headed home from a corner.

glosses: To hit the ball with a stroke that causes a spin, resulting in the ball swerving or staying low after a bounce.
Having the properties of a slice knot.
